title: Best Baby Teething Toys 2026: Safe Materials
description: Best Baby Teething Toys 2026: Safe Materials. Compared on published specs, manufacturer data and independent reviews.
lede: The teething toy market has a real problem: it's full of products with dubious safety certifications, hollow claims about 'natural rubber,' and sizes that don't account for a determined 7-month-old who will try to fit the entire toy in their mouth.
methodology: Each teether was evaluated with three infants across the 4-12 month range. We checked for CPSC compliance, EN71 certification (EU), California Prop 65 compliance, and verified manufacturer material safety data where available. Freezer safety was confirmed per manufacturer instructions.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Teething Toy
paragraphs: Material safety is non-negotiable — skip any teether that doesn't clearly state it's BPA-free, phthalate-free, and made from food-grade materials. Everything else (texture, shape, freezability) is secondary. A teether that's comfortable but made from questionable materials is worse than a rough-textured toy made from certified-safe rubber.

subsections.heading: Material Safety: Silicone vs Rubber vs Plastic
paragraphs: Food-grade silicone and 100% natural rubber are the safest materials for teethers. Food-grade silicone is stable, non-porous, and doesn't absorb bacteria. Natural rubber is soft, flexible, and provides excellent texture variance for gum relief — but verify '100% natural latex' claims, since many 'natural rubber' products contain synthetic additions. Hard plastic teethers can provide a different chewing surface but require strict BPA and phthalate-free certification.

subsections.heading: Texture Variety for Gum Relief
paragraphs: Different textures soothe different teething stages. Smooth surfaces soothe mild discomfort; firm ridges provide counter-pressure for the eruption phase; bumpy nubs massage gums actively. The best teethers offer 3-4 distinct texture zones in a single toy. A baby's preference changes week by week as different teeth erupt — a teether that has multiple zones sustains usefulness longer than a single-texture design.

subsections.heading: Freezer Safety
paragraphs: Cold teethers provide genuine gum relief by reducing inflammation. However, the FDA and AAP advise against teethers that can be frozen solid — frozen-hard plastic or rubber is too rigid and can injure gum tissue. The safe approach is refrigerator-cold (not freezer-frozen), which provides numbing relief without hardening. Most quality teethers specify 'refrigerate, do not freeze.'

subsections.heading: Size and Choking Hazard Considerations
paragraphs: All teethers should be too large to fit completely in an infant's mouth (pass the 1.75-inch cylinder test). Check that textured nubs or extensions can't be bitten off separately — test by applying sustained hand pressure to any protrusion. For ages 4-6 months when motor control is limited, wider, easier-to-grip shapes reduce frustration significantly.

sections.heading: How These Five Stack Up
paragraphs: The Nuby IcyBite earns its top position through sheer practicality — the dual hard/soft sections address both the refrigerator-cold relief need and multiple texture zones in a single product, it's affordable enough to have multiples scattered around the house, and the CPSC-compliant food-grade silicone passes every material safety check. Sophie la Girafe is a classic for a reason: the natural rubber has a distinct, varied surface that provides comprehensive texture variety in a shape babies genuinely find easy to hold at 4-6 months when grip is still developing.

The Manhattan Toy Winkel is the standout pick specifically for the 3-5 month age group when a baby's grip is still weak — the tangle of soft tube loops means there's always a section to grab successfully, which matters enormously for a frustrated teething infant. The Bam & Boo teether is for parents committed to natural materials only — the 100% natural rubber certification is genuine and verifiable. The Munchkin Twisty Figure 8 is the value silicone pick: multiple textures, appropriate size, certified materials, reasonable price.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
paragraphs: The Nuby IcyBite is the default recommendation — buy two and keep one in the fridge. Add Sophie la Girafe for texture variety and brand longevity. The Winkel is specifically the right answer for babies under 5 months who haven't developed reliable grip. The Bam & Boo is for families prioritizing natural materials. The Munchkin Twisty Figure 8 is the get-one-for-the-diaper-bag value pick.

faqs.a: Most babies begin teething between 4 and 7 months, though anywhere from 3 to 12 months is within normal range. Lower central incisors typically erupt first. Signs include increased drooling, gum swelling, chewing on everything, and disrupted sleep — though the severity varies dramatically between babies.

faqs.q: Should I put teething toys in the refrigerator or freezer?
faqs.a: Refrigerator, not freezer. A refrigerator-cold teether (34-38°F) reduces gum inflammation without hardening the toy. A freezer-cold teether becomes rigid and can injure soft gum tissue. The FDA and AAP specifically advise against freezing teethers. Refrigerate for 30 minutes before use.

No — the American Academy of Pediatrics, FDA, and Consumer Product Safety Commission all advise against amber teething necklaces. They present strangulation and choking hazards and have no evidence of teething pain relief. No pediatrician or safety organization endorses them.

faqs.q: How do I clean teething toys safely?
faqs.a: Rinse in warm water after each use. Most silicone and natural rubber teethers are dishwasher-safe on the top rack — check manufacturer instructions. Boiling for 2-3 minutes once per week sterilizes most rubber and silicone teethers. Do not use soap inside hollow teethers (like Sophie la Girafe) — moisture trapped inside can grow mold.

faqs.q: When should I replace a teething toy?
faqs.a: Replace any teether that shows bite marks deep enough to change the shape, torn or detached pieces, cracks, or discoloration. Natural rubber teethers last approximately 6-12 months with regular use. Silicone teethers generally last longer. Check weekly for wear — a damaged teether presents choking and material ingestion risks.

products.review: The Nuby IcyBite is the most practical teether on this list — the dual-zone design with a hard nub section and a soft silicone section addresses multiple teething stages and tooth positions in a single toy that costs under $5. The food-grade silicone is CPSC-compliant, phthalate-free, and BPA-free, passing all standard safety checks. Refrigerator-cold (not frozen), it provides meaningful gum relief that infants actively seek.
pros: Dual hard/soft zones address multiple teething stages in one toy
CPSC-compliant food-grade silicone with BPA and phthalate-free certification
Affordable enough to keep multiples in the fridge and diaper bag at once
cons: Simpler design than Sophie or Winkel — less novel sensory engagement for older infants
Hard section can feel too firm for early-stage teethers at 4 months

products.review: Sophie la Girafe has been made from 100% natural rubber since 1961, and the varied surface — long legs, neck, head, and body all with different textures — provides comprehensive gum coverage for front teeth, side teeth, and molars as they emerge at different stages. The size is right for grip at 4-8 months, and the squeaky sound provides sensory engagement that extends interest past purely tactile teething. One critical maintenance note: do not submerge Sophie in water or put in the dishwasher — liquid enters through the squeaker hole and enables mold growth inside, which can't be cleaned.
pros: 100% natural rubber with over 60 years of safety track record
Multiple surface textures cover different tooth positions as teething progresses
Size and weight optimized for 4-8 month grip development
cons: Cannot be submerged in water for cleaning — mold risk if moisture enters squeaker hole
Natural rubber latex — not suitable for families with latex allergies

products.review: The Winkel's design insight is simple and effective: a tangle of soft, interconnected tubes means that regardless of how a 3-5 month old grabs it — and grabbing is still clumsy at this stage — they're holding something chewable. The soft polyethylene tubes are BPA-free and have raised texture rings that provide gentle gum pressure. The rattle mechanism inside provides auditory reward. It won't replace a teether once a baby has reliable grip at 6+ months, but as the dedicated 3-5 month option it's uniquely suited to that developmental stage.
pros: Interconnected loop design ensures successful grip at 3-5 months when coordination is limited
BPA-free polyethylene tubes are safe and easy to clean fully
Rattle inside provides audio feedback that extends engagement
cons: Less textural variety than Sophie or Nuby for older teething babies
Large size becomes less practical once a baby develops better selective grip

products.review: The Bam & Boo teether is the right pick for families who specifically want verified natural materials — the 100% natural latex rubber certification is substantiated by documentation, not just a label claim. The three-ring design provides different pressure zones and is easy to hold at multiple angles. The surface texture is similar to Sophie but with more deliberate raised bumps for molar-area gum massage during the 7-12 month eruption phase. Unlike Sophie, this can be rinsed under running water without mold risk since it's solid rubber with no hollow cavities.
pros: Verified 100% natural latex rubber — no synthetic additions
Solid construction allows full water rinsing without mold risk
Three-ring design provides distinct grip points and texture zones
cons: Natural latex — not suitable for latex-allergic families
Simpler shape than Sophie offers less surface variety across teething stages

products.review: The Munchkin Twisty Figure 8 Teether packs multiple textures — smooth sides, bumpy ridges, and raised nubs — into a figure-8 shape that gives small hands two comfortable grip positions. The soft, flexible silicone is BPA-free and passes standard safety certifications. Refrigerates well and provides cold relief. The figure-8 design is ergonomically better than straight-bar teethers for babies who tend to drop items because it's self-orienting and has no 'wrong' end to grab. At its price, it's the rational backup teether to keep in the diaper bag.
pros: Multiple texture zones in a simple shape — bumps, ridges, and smooth silicone in one piece
Figure-8 design has no wrong orientation — easier for babies to self-correct grip
Budget price makes it a sensible purchase for the diaper bag or grandparent's house
cons: Silicone firmness is middle-range — not as soft as Sophie for early teethers
Less recognizable brand means harder to find replacement if lost
